content.text: Leyden is a two-player domino game named after the university city in South Holland. It is a variant of the 'Matador' family of domino games, characterized by the 'Rule of Seven'â€”players must build arms from a central spinner by matching adjacent ends so they total exactly seven. The game features special 'Matador' tiles that can be played on any end regardless of the sum rule.

Believed to have developed in the 19th century as a variant of the Matador domino family. The name 'Leyden' (Leiden in Dutch) refers to the university city in South Holland, though the exact historical connection is unclear.
Standard double-six domino set (28 tiles:  through ).
Each player draws 6 tiles. The remaining 16 tiles form the boneyard (stock), placed face-down.

items.text: Matador (Dominoes): The broader family of sum-seven domino games from which Leyden derives.
German Variant: First round begun by player with highest double (not lowest), who may lead any double except 0-0. Winner scores plus total pips; first to 100 points wins (not loses).
Seven-Up Card Game: Related arithmetic card game using similar sum-seven mechanics.
Bergen: Similar Dutch domino variant with different matching rules.
